Rewards are easy to use, though transferring rewards to other CapOne accounts is limited by the account type (kind of annoying). The system has occasional issues, and I've been denied access to my accounts for sometimes hours, though this is not a regular occurrence. My main complaint is in how long it takes to do pretty much anything with Capital One. Transactions take days to post (and you cannot pay for pending transactions as you can with other institutions like Chase). And transferring money into CapOne savings accounts is about a week-long affair. Other than that, nothing terrible to say. I had to contact customer service once-- they were professional and kind. Overall, quicker would be better, but I'm pretty happy with my Capital One accounts right now.

reviews.t: Part Smokescreen, Part Glitch, Part Stonewall...
reviews.x: I wanted to ask about an increase to my credit line and this app told me “Something went wrong. Try again later.” This app will not give you an option to speak with a human representative until AFTER it has initiated a “hard pull” on your credit score! The glitch in the robot’s programming will drag down your credit score without you ever even speaking to an actual person. Once you finally do get a human customer service rep on the phone, all they can do is apologize for the robot! Now I’ve got to send a written dispute to TransUnion via certified mail! Had I spoken to an actual person this minor nightmare would never have happened. My advice to YOU is to use this app for information only. If you have a question regarding your credit, do not speak to a robot or give it any financial information. Get out of the app, and call Capital One customer service and speak with an actual person; they’re actually very knowledgeable and very helpful. - �This app is a minefield. -

I only manage a credit card they the app. I like they keep it simple and is easy to pay, see recent transaction and super easy to log in. They keep it current with the new technology something I really like and is optional. You can choose, depending your device capability, lo use your password, finger print or Face ID. I think you can connect with others account and have a lot more options but I personally haven’t explore it. I love the customer service- is exceptional every time I had call them. They are also very proactive in the account security, they notify you right away if there some unusual activity in your account. I don’t give five star because I think it will be very useful if after each transaction they can give you the remaining balance instead of only a big number after all the transactions on the top of the page. Also I think it will be nice have some type of resource to plan your budgets or stuff like that to help people be more effective in managing their accounts- maybe they have it but not what I am aware off so far. Overall: is a great app and I totally recommended from the credit card point.

I loved cApital one. I always recommend it to people. They are not like BOA that has a lot of hidden charges/fees and rude customer service. Capital One has great customer service although I have just one bad experience from them when I was asking them to help me with a dispute. They were not really frank and honest with me. It was somewhat disorganized the way they handled it and I ended up not getting the money refunded which I think I should have because it is not my fault that the reservation has some issues. They asked me for evidence via the site not my personal email and then after giving it to them, they asked another proof but because I hardly go to the main website, I didn't see the note right away. Then they closed the dispute without properly communicating to me any other way such as via personal email or phone call. So I could have easily given them 5 rating but because of this one major incident, I'm just giving them a 4/5.

Works well. Allows you to do most day-to-day banking activities, including Bill Pay and Mobile Check Deposit. Statements are viewable right within the app. Nice, easy-to-read accounts overview. Convenient login with either a swipe pattern or Touch ID. The app also functions as a two-factor token for the website if you turn that feature on. Overall a satisfying experience as far as mobile banking goes. Some things are missing or awkward: A running balance would be nice, at least in the full transaction log. The "View All" link to get to the full transaction log is very small and hard to see, while there is a big slider to "Lock Your Debit Card" - which of these am I more likely to use on a daily basis? It does not seem possible to set up or modify recurring transfers in the app, only on the website. Paper check images are not available here (nor on the recently updated website for that matter), and check memos are absent. (I know, paper checks, what am I thinking?! So last century!) Most of the actions available in the transaction details seem like odd things that one would rarely ever need, for instance "Report Problem" (are there that many problematic transactions?), "Call Merchant" etc. You can even "Report Problem" for an interest deposit or a transfer you made between your own accounts! I also find the horizontal band of transactions in the account view not particularly useful since the small tiles contain hardly more information than the transaction amount. In particular, for transfers there isn't enough space to show the name of the transfer account. Confusingly, the band is labeled "Recent Transactions," but it also shows scheduled (future) transactions, and the only way to tell the two apart is by the small date - how about color coding or a hatch pattern? Update: Version 5.25.1 seems to fix the crashing problem that apparently lots of people had with 5.25.0. Seven days to fix a blocking bug. I'll be sure to check the reviews before updating next time ...

reviews.t: Great app, but please bring back the essentials.
reviews.x: The app works well but innovations took away some essential capabilities. 1) With Zelle it is no longer possible to set up recurring automatic payments. That is possible only by mailing paper checks. Paper checks are not a part of my life anymore. I, and hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers, pay rent to a roommate who in turn pays the landlord. The loss of recurring person-to-person payments is the loss of an incredibly useful feature. 2) The app no longer allows memos on payments, whether by check or Zelle. Memos are very useful and the loss has caused me much more work when reconciling health payments. For example, I see my therapist multiple times a month. She is terrible at tracking bills and payments. Now I must do much more sleuthing when checking which appointments I have paid for and which I have yet to pay for. 3) No more messages?? I had a message from customer service to track down one of said payments, and it's now gone. I do not have time to wait on the phone through multiple prompts nor do I want to text a robot about my money. Being able to send a message that a human would answer was incredibly convenient and now impossible. I love my capital one bank accounts and credit card. I hope these hugely convenient capabilities return!
